terra.problem: John's identification as the man who baptized Jesus is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The comparison doesn't fit: being stuck in a dusty spot doesn't explain a pull to return to it. His drawer reference also lacks enough context.
The junk drawer reference isn't explained for a baker who doesn't know his backstory.
The explanation is generic and repeats Capernaum without adding much personality or insight.
The last sentence presents Isaiah's words as being about a moment like Papa Dorin's rescue. Matthew connects their fulfillment to Jesus living in Capernaum.
The text says the brothers followed at once, but doesn't say whether they asked for a minute.
A whole lot of nets and a family business add details the text doesn't give.
Saying just the brothers and their father were in the boat rules out others, while the text only names those three.
The claim that city gates were busy places is outside the passage and needs a reference.
Calling the journey a full day's work adds a time frame the passage doesn't give.
